# `aitbc market gpu buy`

Fund a quoted GPU rental (native escrow or EVM contract).

## Usage

```bash
aitbc market gpu buy [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--gpu-id` | text | — | yes | GPU registry ID |
| `--buyer-id` | text | — | yes | Buyer client ID from the quote (native rail: the funding wallet address 0x...) |
| `--job-id` | text | — | yes | Job ID from the quote response |
| `--duration-hours` | float | — | yes | Rental duration in hours |
| `--settlement` | choice | `native` | no | Settlement rail |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet name for signing |
| `--wallet-path` | text | — | no | Direct wallet file path |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--energy-quote` | text | — | no | JSON file containing the energy quote |
| `--max-ait` | float | — | no | Maximum AIT buyer cap |
| `--yes` | flag | `false` | no | Skip confirmation prompt |
| `--json-output` | flag | `false` | no | Output raw JSON |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc market gpu buy --gpu-id <gpu_id> --buyer-id <buyer_id> --job-id <job_id> --duration-hours <duration_hours>
```
